featured_reviews.name: Pooja Karambelkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Edited to add a photo of the clinics reply on my review.

The clinic owner has publicly named my business and made allegations of fake reviews and misuse of influence, amounting to defamation. These claims are incorrect and unrelated to the care my pet received.
My review reflects my personal experience and is supported by medical records.
I will not engage further and will allow appropriate authorities to review the matter.
The case is already under multiple statutory body investigation.

I am writing this review as an informed and responsible bird parent, sharing my personal experience in good faith.
My macaw was treated at this clinic over multiple visits for an injury. During the course of treatment, I observed a steady and concerning deterioration in his condition despite regular follow-ups. I repeatedly raised concerns about pain, bandaging, and worsening symptoms, but felt these concerns were not adequately acknowledged or addressed at the time.
Over several visits, I also noticed that day-to-day treatment and follow-ups were frequently handled by junior staff or interns, while the senior veterinarian whose expertise the clinic is widely known for was not consistently present. As the guardian of an exotic bird requiring specialised care, this raised serious concerns for me regarding continuity, supervision, and decision-making during treatment.
Eventually, due to the worsening condition and my growing distress, I sought care elsewhere. I was then informed that significant and irreversible damage had already occurred, leading to permanent consequences for my bird. This outcome was devastating.
What compounded this experience was the lack of clear communication and accountability afterward. My attempts to seek explanations and understand how the situation had progressed were not met with transparency or clarity.
I want to be clear that this review reflects my personal experience and perceptions only, and is not a statement of legal findings. The matter is currently under review by the appropriate statutory authorities.
I am sharing this so other pet parents—especially those with exotic or avian companions—can remain vigilant, ask detailed questions about who is providing care, seek clarity on treatment decisions, and consider second opinions when they feel uncertain.

This review is written in good faith, with the hope that transparency leads to reflection, accountability, and improved care standards.

featured_reviews.name: Saudnya Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is an old one, but I HAD to say it so here we go.

I crossed paths with Rina Dev about 10 years ago when she worked at Deepa Katyal’s clinic in Chembur. My 12 week old pup was pretty sick & towards the end of his treatment, my family & I were needing to be out of town for a few days. I was looking for reliable boarding options for my baby but Rina “VOLUNTEERED” to baby sit him at a per-day price that she was comfortable at (which is totally fine btw). BUT, while he was there, not only did she fail to give him his medication on time, but also “conveniently” forgot the remaining set of his meds back at her place, when I came to pick him up at the clinic. Which is fine I guess - happens at times to all of us. But the least she could’ve done is apologize. I’m not saying I expected a bunch of tears & a heart full of regret; but even something casual & breezy to just acknowledge it would’ve helped — especially when I was traveling all the way from the other end of the city, & I HAD TO COME BACK TO THE CLINIC THE NEXT DAY to restock one of his meds that she had forgotten back at her house (it was only available at deepa’s clinic at the time). In the meantime, my pup had to skip a couple of doses again, until I restocked it.

Long story short - I’ve had a bad experience with Rina Dev that’s got nothing to do with her technical skillset, but her absolute LACK OF ACCOUNTABILITY. (hate to break it to you princess - it’s equally important)

featured_reviews.review_text:
As a pet parent, I’m sure many of you will understand the kind of fear and helplessness we feel when something isn’t right with our baby. I went through exactly that when my 14-year-old feline, Goldie, was diagnosed with a serious tumour on her left paw. Those days were filled with worry, questions, and uncertainty.

All we knew was that we needed the right oncologist — someone we could trust completely. That’s when we found the incredible team at Superpets, and from that very first visit, everything began to feel a little lighter.

From explaining the diagnosis and possible causes, to guiding us through every test, every step was handled with so much patience, clarity, and compassion. What truly stood out was how reassuring the entire team was — always available to answer questions, clear doubts, and take that extra effort to make both us and Goldie feel comfortable.

The journey — from diagnosis, to surgery, to post-operative care and stitch removal — was smoother than we could have ever hoped for. Every decision they made felt right, thoughtful, and in Goldie’s best interest.

A special note of gratitude to Dr. Pratyush, Dr. Vasudha, and Dr. Gauri — you are truly angels in disguise. The care, dedication, and gentleness with which you handled Goldie means the world to us. It’s not just medical expertise, but your genuine love for animals that makes all the difference.

I must admit, I was initially skeptical about traveling all the way from the suburbs to Bandra for treatment — but today, I can say with complete conviction that every visit, every effort, was absolutely worth it.

What touched me deeply was that even after a month, Dr. Pratyush personally followed up to check on Goldie’s health. That level of care is rare and speaks volumes about the kind of people they are — not just doctors, but true lifesavers.

This entire experience has been a journey of gratitude. People like them are not just treating animals — they are healing families.

Thank you, Superpets team, from the bottom of my heart, for taking such beautiful care of our baby.

Forever grateful. 🙏🏻

featured_reviews.name: Smitaa Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a blessing. My German shepherd champ was taken to super pets in an emergency situation. He had developed something called GDV. I was unaware if this situation being a pet parent since more than 17 years now (I have had pets since several years) After taking him to vetic hospital for emergency (which was extremely careless and didn’t even treat it like emergency) post his X-ray on recommendation from some friends I rushed him to super pets. They immediately took charge of the situation. He underwent operation and was discharged in 5 days. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolute lifesavers – Wild Vets Bandra gave my cat Mao Singh a second chance at life!

I can’t thank the team at Wild Vets in Bandra enough**

A few weeks ago, my beloved feline Mao Singh (my ginger-white drama queen) suddenly became critically ill – lethargic, not eating, and hiding all day. I rushed her to Wild Vets and from the moment we walked in, I knew she was in the best hands.
Dr. Nidhi immediately took charge — calm, thorough, and incredibly compassionate. They didn’t waste a second: full in-house blood work, urine analysis, stroke checks (I think they meant biochemistry/profile), and ultrasound (USG) were all done under one roof on the spot. No running around to different labs, no waiting days for results – everything was diagnosed and treated the same day. That comprehensive in-house facility literally saved precious time and, I genuinely believe, saved Mao Singh’s life. Within hours they had her on IV fluids, targeted medication, and close monitoring.
The entire staff was outstanding — special shoutout to Bhaskar and the rest of the assistants who handled my stressed-out cat with so much gentleness and care, keeping me updated every step of the way, even after hours. The clinic is spotless, well-equipped (dedicated cat consult room, ultrasound room, pharmacy stocked with premium medicines), and clearly designed with pets’ comfort in mind — separate dog den and cat corner to reduce stress.

Yes, Wild Vets is not the cheapest vet in town, but when it’s your family member on the line, quality comes at a price — and it’s worth every single rupee. I’d rather pay for expertise, speed, and state-of-the-art facilities than take risks elsewhere.
Today Mao Singh is back home, eating like a champ, zooming around, and giving me her signature judgmental stares

❤️ Thank you from the bottom of my heart to Dr. Nidhi, Dr. Deb, Bhaskar, and the entire Wild Vets family. You didn’t just treat my cat — you gave her (and me) hope and a future. Forever grateful. If you love your pet, this is the only place in Bandra (and probably Mumbai) I’d trust blindly.
Highly recommended — 5 stars aren’t enough! 🐱💙

featured_reviews.name: Neha Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
❌ WARNING: DO NOT TRUST THIS CLINIC WITH YOUR PET’S LIFE ❌
If you love your pets, STAY AWAY. This is not a veterinary clinic; it is a money-making machine that uses fear tactics to scam honest pet owners.

On January 23rd, 2026, I brought my pet in for a blood test. The next day, they claimed his creatinine was 4.8 mg/dL (the normal range is 0.5–1.5). They looked me in the eye and told me my "little kid" was in critical condition and needed 10 days of IV drips, which would have cost me 25k–30k.

My pet looked perfectly fine, so I followed my gut and got a second opinion. I took him to a family vet on January 25th for a re-test. The result? 0.9 mg/dL. PERFECTLY NORMAL.

How is this possible?

It is medically impossible for a creatinine level to drop from a fatal 4.8 to a healthy 0.9 in 24 hours without any treatment.

Either their lab equipment is dangerously broken, they mixed up the samples, or—more likely—they fabricated the results to extort 30,000 from a worried family.

They were willing to put my healthy pet through 10 days of unnecessary, invasive medical procedures just to pad their bank account. Their "explanation" in their email was nothing but excuses.

DO NOT let them scare you into paying for treatments your pet doesn't need. They are predatory, unethical, and dangerous. Go literally anywhere else.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had a very terrible experience at this hospital. The staff is unsupportive and they seemed indifferent to my concern. I went there for my cat, he had jaundice. featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

featured_reviews.name: Omkar Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have visited Critter Care Clinic twice over the past year for two different pets, and both experiences were excellent.

My turtle had a severe eye infection and was unable to open her eyes, while my cockatiel was attacked by a crow and suffered an injured leg that left him bleeding and unable to stand properly. The doctors were incredibly caring, knowledgeable, and quick to suggest the right treatment for both of them.

Thanks to their expertise, my turtle can now open her eyes again, and my cockatiel is healthy, active, and moving around happily. I’m truly grateful for the care and attention they provided. Highly recommended for anyone looking for compassionate and reliable veterinary care for their pets.

Ps : You can see my cockatiel is now moving happily

featured_reviews.name: jagandeep sandhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
I travelled all the way from Punjab to get my bunny treated by Dr. Hena. My bunny had been suffering from a dental disease for almost a year, and within just two days she solved a problem that no one else could. We got a dental surgery done, and now my bunny is eating like never before.

I highly recommend Dr. Hena — she is incredibly empathetic, listens with patience, and answers even your most idiotic questions with kindness and clarity. Truly grateful.

featured_reviews.name: Vinay Sumrraa
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best veterinary clinics I’ve ever been to!
The entire team at Critter Care Veterinary Clinic is amazing — Dr. Henna, Dr. Ruchi, Varsha madam, and Tekraj bhai are always so helpful and compassionate. They even attend calls late at night and never hesitate to guide or support. Their kindness towards stray animals is truly heartwarming, often giving concessions and going out of their way to help.
Highly recommend Critter Care for their dedication, care, and love for animals❤️

featured_reviews.name: Sneha Mohanty
featured_reviews.review_text: While I'm someone who almost NEVER writes a negative review, but I do make it a point to call out selfish clinics when it comes to my furbaby. Here is my experience for you: I'm not sure how good of a get dr Henna is, however, the clinic staff is EXTREMELY rude and unprofessional. You almost never get a teleconsultation. While teleconsult charges are way higher than regular market standard, however, you get very very rude responses from the clinic when all you're doing is try to get an appointment for your dying pet. 1. You almost never get an appointment here. 2. Even if you have a follow up, youll get rude responses.

featured_reviews.name: Shaifali Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
What started as a loving welcome for my turtle turned into a very upsetting experience. Despite owning my turtle for 17 years and knowing its needs, the clinic forced unnecessary tests worth ₹4,000 (blood tests and x ray) and charged ₹900 just for checking it.

When I objected, the assistant arrogantly stated that their protocol is to “do tests and make money first, then treat the pet.” That was shocking and heartbreaking as a pet parent.

Please don’t be fooled by their sweet talk. In my experience, they care more about money than animals. Avoid if you truly love your pet

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Jaswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Most insensitive approach by doc. My Guinea pig was suffering from broken hip bone plus stones in bladder. He was active and was walking on four legs before I took him to the doc . After X ray and check up I got him home and I noticed that he is falling and not able to walk only. When I  called at clinic they are not willing to accept that they had mishandled my pet and doc claimed that he was walking fine.
I spoke to the doc on phone but doc said what do you want me do. Instead of showing any sort of sympathy towards a pet ..doc attitude was pathetic. No remorse , no accountability and zero emotions.
As a pet parent you don’t loose your pet by mishandling, you loose faith and heart in the process of loss.

featured_reviews.name: Udit Khanna
featured_reviews.review_text: Dr. Henna was very loving and professional and told me dos and don'ts for my pup. There was a guinea pig, a bird, and a cat at the clinic as well so I'm pretty sure she can help you with any animal. Her charges were reasonable and totally worth the amount of time and care she took. Thank you!

featured_reviews.name: Darsh Dodia
featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.review_text: There's nothing that I want to say. All I know is I lost my pet. He could have probably lived for a few more months or years. His kidneys had already failed.

featured_reviews.review_text: Not recommended. Prescribed high dose of insulin for borderline diabetes due to which our dog experienced seizures. Our dog was 10 years old and we lost him last month due to kidney failure.
